report:
**Conclusion: the claim is well supported** for postmenopausal women with osteoporosis, particularly those at high fracture risk.

The pivotal evidence is the phase 3 ACTIVE randomized trial (2,463 women; mean age 69), which compared daily subcutaneous abaloparatide 80 µg with placebo for 18 months. New *morphometric* vertebral fractures were substantially less frequent with abaloparatide: 0.6% versus 4.2% with placebo—an absolute reduction of 3.6 percentage points and relative reduction of about 86%. The trial also found fewer nonvertebral fractures.  
https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/fullarticle/2544640  
https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27533157/

The FDA label independently summarizes the pivotal trial and reports consistent fracture-risk reductions across subgroups, including age, previous fractures, and baseline bone mineral density. This supports applicability across the indicated high-risk postmenopausal population.  
https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2017/208743lbl.pdf

Supporting synthesis is consistent: a 2024 systematic review/meta-analysis concluded that abaloparatide protects women with postmenopausal osteoporosis and reduces vertebral-fracture risk.  
https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38307725/

**Important qualifications:** Evidence directly establishes benefit over **18 months** versus placebo, using radiographically detected vertebral fractures; it does not mean every individual will benefit by the same amount. The treatment entails daily injections and has risks/contraindications, so it is generally reserved for people at high or very high fracture risk rather than used routinely for all osteoporosis.
